title: Christmas on the road
setup_text: Both sides of the family want to see your child at Christmas. The homes are far apart, and two visits in one day would be tiring.

choices.label: Visit one family and call the other
choices.outcome_text: One home got the long visit; the other joined by phone. There were already questions about next Christmas.

choices.label: Make shorter visits to both
choices.outcome_text: Both homes got a visit, and the day involved a lot of packing and travelling. The journey made for a long day.

choices.label: Stay home and invite relatives over
choices.outcome_text: Christmas happened at home, with an open invitation and a pot on the stove. Some relatives could come; others joined by phone.

title: Sunday together
setup_text: You each have a church you feel at home in. With a young child, attending both services every Sunday would make for a very long morning.

choices.label: Attend one church together for now
choices.outcome_text: The family found a regular Sunday rhythm in one place. There were still people at the other church to call and visit.

choices.label: Alternate between the two churches
choices.outcome_text: Sunday mornings had two familiar destinations. It took more planning, and both congregations got to know your child.

choices.label: Keep separate services for now
choices.outcome_text: Each parent kept a familiar service in the week. The family had less time together that morning and met again afterwards.

title: The advice at bedtime
setup_text: A relative who helps with the baby suggests a different bedtime routine. Their help matters, but the current routine has finally begun to work.

choices.label: Try the relative’s suggestion for a week
choices.outcome_text: The evenings changed for a while. The family kept notes on what worked and made time to talk again.

choices.label: Keep the routine and explain why
choices.outcome_text: The familiar bedtime stayed. The conversation took care, and the relative continued to help in other ways.

choices.label: Ask the relative to help with another part
choices.outcome_text: Bedtime stayed as it was, while the relative took on another task. There was more to coordinate, but help remained close.

title: A place at nursery
setup_text: A nursery you like has offered a place, but its fees would mean spending less at home. A less expensive nursery is farther away.

choices.label: Choose the nearby nursery and adjust spending
choices.outcome_text: The shorter trip became part of the week. The family made room in the budget by putting some other plans on hold.

choices.label: Choose the farther nursery
choices.outcome_text: The fees left more room in the budget. Mornings started earlier to make the longer journey.

choices.label: Wait and keep the current care for now
choices.outcome_text: The current arrangement continued while the family saved and looked again. The nursery place went to another child.

title: Two school gates
setup_text: One school is close enough to walk to. Another has a teaching style you like, but the drive would change every working morning.

choices.label: Choose the school nearby
choices.outcome_text: The school run became a walk. The family stayed in touch with teachers about what happened in the classroom.

choices.label: Choose the school farther away
choices.outcome_text: The preferred teaching style came with an earlier start. The family made a new plan for the drive.

choices.label: Visit both schools again with your child
choices.outcome_text: The decision took another week. Your child met both places, and the family had more questions to ask.

title: Whose house this Christmas?
setup_text: Your child is excited to see both sets of grandparents. Each family has planned Christmas lunch at the same time.

choices.label: Spend this Christmas with one side
choices.outcome_text: One table had the long visit this year. The other family got a call and a plan for another day together.

choices.label: Divide the day between both homes
choices.outcome_text: There were greetings at both houses and a long journey in between. Lunch happened in stages.

choices.label: Host a meal at home on another day
choices.outcome_text: Christmas lunch stayed with one set of plans, and a shared meal followed at home. Hosting took work, but gave everyone more time.

title: Two Sunday communities
setup_text: Your churches both have children’s activities. One is close to home; the other is where relatives worship and your child knows the songs.

choices.label: Choose the church close to home
choices.outcome_text: Sunday travel became simpler. The family kept visits to the other congregation for some special days.

choices.label: Choose the church with family
choices.outcome_text: Familiar relatives and songs became part of Sunday. The longer trip needed planning each week.

choices.label: Alternate for a trial period
choices.outcome_text: The child spent time in both communities. A check-in was planned after a few weeks, though the changing routine took getting used to.

title: The words for home
setup_text: Your child is picking up English at school. A grandparent hopes they will also learn the family language, which needs practice at home.

choices.label: Set aside time for the family language
choices.outcome_text: A few familiar words found their way into the week. Finding time to practise meant moving another activity.

choices.label: Ask the grandparent to share stories
choices.outcome_text: Stories travelled between generations, sometimes over the phone. Everyone worked around the grandparent’s availability.

choices.label: Use whichever language comes naturally
choices.outcome_text: Conversations stayed easy and mixed. The family language came up less often, but the door stayed open to learning more.

title: The birthday list
setup_text: Your child wants a birthday party and has named the whole class. Your budget would cover a small gathering or a simple treat for everyone.

choices.label: Invite a few friends for a small party
choices.outcome_text: A few children gathered at home. There was time for each friend, and some classmates were not on the list.

choices.label: Send a simple treat for the class
choices.outcome_text: The celebration reached the whole class without a party at home. The day was simpler than the party your child imagined.

choices.label: Make a family celebration this year
choices.outcome_text: The birthday stayed close to home and within the budget. Your child helped choose how to mark the day with family.

title: After the school run
setup_text: Your child comes home with a small school activity and wants to play immediately. Dinner and bedtime are not far away.

choices.label: Do the activity before play
choices.outcome_text: The activity was done while the table was clear. Play started later and had to fit into the time left.

choices.label: Play first and return to the activity
choices.outcome_text: There was time to unwind first. The family came back to the activity later, closer to bedtime.

choices.label: Ask the teacher about a manageable routine
choices.outcome_text: The evening stayed simple while a note went to school. A conversation about what fits at home began the next day.

title: Picture day hair
setup_text: School picture day is coming. Your child wants one hairstyle; a relative has offered to make a different style that takes longer.

choices.label: Choose the style your child asked for
choices.outcome_text: Picture day began with a familiar style. The relative found another day to share the style they had in mind.

choices.label: Accept the relative’s offer
choices.outcome_text: The styling took longer and became time spent together. Your child had a different look for the photograph.

choices.label: Find a shorter version together
choices.outcome_text: Everyone looked for a style that could be finished sooner. It took some discussion, and the morning had a little more room.

title: Room for a cousin
setup_text: A cousin is visiting for a week and needs a place to sleep. Your child likes the cousin but is unsure about sharing their room.

choices.label: Make space in the child’s room
choices.outcome_text: The cousins shared a room for the week. Bedtime became livelier, and each child needed a little space during the day.

choices.label: Make a bed in the sitting room
choices.outcome_text: Your child kept their room while the sitting room became a bedroom at night. The family rearranged its evening routine.

choices.label: Ask the children to plan the space together
choices.outcome_text: The children chose where to put the bags and bedding with grown-up help. The planning took time, and both had a say in the visit.

title: A new uniform
setup_text: Your child has grown out of a school uniform. A relative offers a clean hand-me-down; your child has noticed classmates wearing new ones.

choices.label: Use the hand-me-down and adjust it
choices.outcome_text: The uniform got a few alterations and another year of use. There was money left for other school needs.

choices.label: Buy a new uniform
choices.outcome_text: A new uniform went into the school bag. The family moved another purchase to make room for it.

choices.label: Let your child help choose between options
choices.outcome_text: The family looked at the cost and the fit together. Choosing took longer, and your child had a voice in what came home.

title: The Sunday invitation
setup_text: A family celebration falls on the same morning as an activity your child has been looking forward to at church. Both matter to your family.

choices.label: Attend the church activity first
choices.outcome_text: The child took part in the activity. The family arrived at the celebration later and caught the rest of the gathering.

choices.label: Go to the family celebration
choices.outcome_text: The family spent the morning with relatives. The missed activity was disappointing, and the child heard about it from friends later.

choices.label: Ask whether you can join part of each
choices.outcome_text: The day needed careful timing and a few phone calls. The family shared some time in both places without staying for everything.
